PullRequest.Title: agentHost: add session and chat rename tools
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #329380

Adds Agent Host server-side tools for renaming a session and an individual chat.

- Adds `rename_session` and `rename_chat` with target validation, live state propagation, persistence, and provider-neutral display.
- Tracks title provenance so provisional/generated, agent-authored, and user-authored titles remain distinguishable. Tool calls themselves are authoritative, allowing explicit later rename requests to replace existing titles.
- Adds an experimental active-agent naming flow. It defaults off on Stable and on for non-Stable builds, synchronizes live for newly created sessions/chats, and retains utility-model title generation when disabled.
- Gives new conversations a readable provisional title and instructs the active agent to gather context, then rename before its first final response.
- Dynamically filters server tools per newly materialized provider session across Copilot, Claude, and Codex.
- Preserves complete agent-supplied titles while retaining concise 1–4 word guidance.

Validation:
- `npm run compile-client`
- `npm run hygiene`
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- Targeted Agent Host title, service, protocol, provider, and server-tool tests
- Coverage tests for dynamic advertisement/disabled execution and end-to-end rename propagation/persistence

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The automatic reminder, tool dispatch, unconditional list call, AgentService fan-out, per-session database reads, and Copilot provider IPC are all directly traced. Exact per-provider duration varies, but the O(S) critical-path mechanism is unambiguous.
Findings.PerformanceResource: SQLite/filesystem operations and provider IPC calls
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each automatic current-session rename performs O(S) metadata work for S registered sessions: one registry query, per-session database/provider-data reads, per-session provider metadata lookups, and another per-session metadata overlay read; concurrent lookups are launched with Promise.all.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: The first response is delayed before it can finish, with latency and I/O/IPC load growing with the user's accumulated session count.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR there was no automatic rename tool call at the end of a new session's first request, so that request did not enumerate the entire session catalog merely to rename itself.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new rename_session implementation always awaits accessor.listSessions(), even when the tool omitted session and currentSession already identifies the target; the new first-request reminder explicitly asks the agent to make exactly this call.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `const sessions = await accessor.listSessions();` at RIGHT line 825 is unconditional in the newly introduced automatic rename tool, despite `currentSession` already being passed by the changed dispatch path.
Findings.Title: Avoid scanning the full session catalog for an in-place rename
Findings.Impact: With tens or hundreds of saved sessions, every newly created session's first response can trigger a burst of provider metadata calls and per-session SQLite reads and must wait for the slowest one before the rename tool returns and the model can produce its final response. The sibling rename_chat path has the same unconditional catalog scan for current peer chats.
Findings.Evidence: applyRenameSessionTool line 825 calls listSessions before resolving the already-supplied currentSession. AgentService.listSessions reads the global registry, maps every registered session through _registeredSessionMetadata, and then opens every returned session database for getMetadataObject. For Copilot, _registeredSessionMetadata reaches CopilotAgent.getChatMetadata, which calls client.getSessionMetadata over the provider boundary for each session; Codex can similarly reach _readSession/thread reads for non-live entries. AgentHostSessionTitleController injects a reminder requiring rename_session on the first active-agent request, making this scan part of the normal first-response path rather than an explicit catalog operation.
Findings.Recommendation: Resolve and validate the current-session/current-peer case directly from the current state (or a targeted metadata accessor), and call listSessions only when an explicit cross-session URI must be resolved. Preserve the full validation path for explicit targets.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The launcher-to-converter call path and unconditional callback are explicit, and JSON.stringify necessarily scales with the prompt-bearing input. Only the exact size distribution of user prompts is uncertain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU time and temporary strings proportional to the user prompt payload
Findings.PerformanceScaling: One JSON serialization occurs for every Copilot user prompt, with CPU and allocated bytes growing linearly with prompt size; this repeats across all turns and concurrent chats even after naming is complete or disabled.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Large pasted prompts incur avoidable synchronous CPU work and allocation/GC pressure before the SDK can continue processing the turn.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The UserPromptSubmitted handler was installed only when plugin prompt commands existed, so sessions without those commands did not stringify the hook input at all.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The broadened condition installs the handler whenever the internal title callback exists, and CopilotSessionLauncher now always supplies that callback. The handler immediately runs JSON.stringify(input) even when promptCommands is empty and the callback returns no additional context.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The changed condition at RIGHT line 438 expands execution of the existing JSON.stringify block from sessions with actual prompt hook commands to every Copilot session because the PR also unconditionally wires onUserPromptSubmitted.
Findings.Title: Do not serialize every Copilot prompt when no prompt hook needs stdin
Findings.Impact: All Copilot turns now copy/serialize the full prompt object solely for a command loop that is usually empty. Large code/log pastes amplify the added latency and GC work, while ordinary turns pay the fixed handler and serialization cost indefinitely.
Findings.Evidence: RIGHT line 438 makes editTrackingHooks.onUserPromptSubmitted sufficient to install the handler. CopilotSessionLauncher always passes that function. Inside the handler, `const stdin = JSON.stringify(input)` runs before iterating `promptCommands ?? []`; CopilotAgentSession.handleUserPromptSubmitted often returns undefined once no rename instruction is present, but the serialization has already happened.
Findings.Recommendation: Only compute `stdin` inside a `promptCommands?.length` branch (or lazily on the first command), then return the internal additional-context callback directly when there are no shell commands.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The synchronous call sequence and exact INSERT multiplicity are directly visible in the changed methods. Storage latency varies, but the repeated I/O and new lifecycle wait are certain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Per-session SQLite INSERT operations, database references, and queued write promises
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The cost repeats for every newly seeded or refined session/chat title. A fresh active-agent session issues three separate metadata writes for one fallback title, while a successful utility-generated title now issues source plus title/source writes after an earlier source write, versus one final title write before the PR.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Title creation produces 3-4x metadata write traffic, increasing filesystem I/O and queue contention and extending deletion/idle-eviction waits that now drain pending session writes.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Applying a fallback title did not write metadata, and successful utility title generation persisted the final custom-title key once.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: _applySeedTitle now immediately writes the auto source. The active path then calls markTitleAuto, whose _persistAutoTitle writes both title and the same source as two more independent setMetadata calls. Utility generation similarly writes source in apply and then writes title plus source again in persist.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added source persistence at RIGHT line 219 duplicates the source write performed by the newly expanded `_persistAutoTitle`; this turns one logical title update into multiple physical metadata writes.
Findings.Title: Persist title provenance once instead of issuing duplicate SQLite writes
Findings.Impact: Every first session/chat title creates multiple serialized SQLite writes for the same provenance value. These writes are fire-and-forget but retain database references and are explicitly awaited by the new whenIdle calls during eviction/deletion, so the amplification affects I/O throughput and lifecycle latency.
Findings.Evidence: RIGHT line 219 adds `_persistAutoTitleSource` to the common session apply path. seedTitleFromFirstMessage immediately follows that apply with markTitleAuto in active mode; markTitleAuto calls _persistAutoTitle, which invokes persistSessionMetadata separately for customTitle and customTitleSource. In utility mode, _generateTitle invokes apply and then persist consecutively, causing the source write in both callbacks. SessionDatabase.setMetadata serializes each as a distinct INSERT.
Findings.Recommendation: Commit title and provenance together once at the persistence point, using the new setMetadataValues transaction/helper where ordering matters. Keep in-memory provenance during apply and remove duplicate source-only writes unless a path truly has no subsequent title persistence.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The full-input allocations and pre-send call path are explicit. User prompt sizes vary, so severity is low, but large pasted prompts are a realistic supported input.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Per-code-point array elements and copied strings derived from the full first user prompt
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Allocation grows O(N) with the complete first prompt even though only 40 or 200 code points can appear in the title; the active path additionally slices and joins the entire remainder while looking for a word boundary.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Large pasted first prompts create avoidable memory churn and synchronous CPU/GC work before the request is sent to the provider.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The normalizer collapsed whitespace and used string.slice(0, 200), which did not allocate an array entry for every code point in the full prompt.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The changed normalizer calls Array.from on the entire normalized prompt before slicing to maxLength. The new active-agent normalizer repeats this full materialization and can also copy/join all characters after position 40.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 174 replaces the prior bounded string slice with a full code-point array allocation on the first-message hot path.
Findings.Title: Bound Unicode title normalization before materializing prompt characters
Findings.Impact: A first request containing a large pasted log, source file, or generated text allocates a full code-point array solely to derive a short display title, delaying turn startup and increasing young-generation GC pressure.
Findings.Evidence: RIGHT line 174 materializes `Array.from(text.trim().replace(...))` before applying the 200-character cap. The adjacent active path creates `characters = Array.from(normalized)` and later `characters.slice(40).join('')`, although its output target is only 40 characters. seedTitleFromFirstMessage runs synchronously from ChatTurnStarted before provider send setup.
Findings.Recommendation: Collapse/iterate code points incrementally and stop once the output cap plus the needed next-word boundary is known; do not build an array or joined suffix for the entire prompt.

Scenarios.Scenario: First request in a newly created default session with active-agent naming enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The host seeds a provisional title, awaits title-source preparation, sends the prompt, and instructs the model to call rename_session before its final response. The rename tool must finish its catalog scan and atomic title persistence before the model can continue to the final response.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One query per rename tool invocation
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Used for explicit catalog operations, not automatically on every new session's first response
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks construction of the catalog needed by the rename tool

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check/open each session database and read provider data plus metadata overlays
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Multiple checks/queries for each of S registered sessions, after provider filtering
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The first response did not invoke listSessions solely to rename its current session
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The rename waits for all per-session reads

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch provider session metadata, including Copilot client.getSessionMetadata for each registered Copilot session
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to one provider call per registered session; effective count follows the provider mix and live-session fast paths
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No automatic current-session rename placed this full provider metadata fan-out on the first-response path
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The rename and therefore first final response wait for the slowest provider lookup

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One transaction with two INSERTs per successful rename
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Utility title persistence was fire-and-forget and did not gate the first final response
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before the tool returns; fixed cardinality and appropriate for durability

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number S of registered sessions accumulated across providers; the automatic flow invokes one rename per new session, and each scan processes all S sessions after registry filtering.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: AgentService uses Promise.all across all registered sessions and another Promise.all for per-session overlays, so per-session filesystem/database/provider work is burst concurrently without a limiter. Metadata writes for the renamed session are serialized by that SessionDatabase's metadata sequencer.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no result cache or request coalescing for listSessions. Warm per-session database references can avoid reopening SQLite connections, but tryOpenDatabase still checks file existence and each call executes metadata queries; provider metadata may be served from live state for some Codex sessions, while Copilot still performs getSessionMetadata IPC for each listed session.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the reminder, tool dispatch, unconditional listSessions call, per-session fan-out, and final-response dependency are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact delay depends on catalog size, provider mix, disk speed, and whether sessions are live, but users with tens or hundreds of sessions are realistic and the O(S) fan-out is certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable high-severity boundary fan-out because an in-place rename now performs catalog-wide I/O/IPC on the first-response critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: First request in a newly created peer chat with active-agent naming enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The peer-chat prompt receives a rename_chat reminder; the model's rename_chat tool call must list sessions, resolve the chat, verify it (usually from live state), persist title/source, and return before final response.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerate metadata for all registered sessions before resolving the current peer chat
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No automatic peer-chat rename or catalog scan existed
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks tool completion and the first peer-chat final response

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read peerChats when live state cannot establish existence
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero for live peers; one metadata read for a non-live target
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks persistence only on the cold/non-live path

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist peer title and source atomically
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No server-side peer rename transaction existed

Scenarios.ScalingInput: S registered sessions for the unconditional catalog scan; peer-chat count matters only for the in-memory `.some` existence check or one persisted peer-catalog read when the session is not live.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The same unbounded Promise.all catalog fan-out applies. Peer existence is an in-memory linear scan for a live session, otherwise one session-database read.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No catalog cache/coalescing. A live peer avoids the persisted peerChats read; a restored/non-live target reads the persisted catalog once.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the unconditional list call and automatic reminder are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Peer chats are less frequent than default sessions, but the same session-count scaling applies whenever the flow is used.
Scenarios.Verdict: Covered by the catalog-scan finding; not submitted separately to avoid duplicating the same mechanism.

Scenarios.Scenario: Copilot prompt submission after provider session materialization
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The SDK invokes onUserPromptSubmitted before continuing the prompt. The host handler serializes its full input, runs any configured prompt commands, then returns optional title context.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per Copilot prompt; bytes are O(N) in prompt size
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Without an actual plugin prompt hook, no handler was installed and no serialization occurred
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous CPU/allocation occurs before the hook can return and prompt processing proceeds

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Execute configured plugin prompt hook commands
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero in the reported common case; one sequential subprocess per configured command when present
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same configured commands already ran sequentially
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing behavior when commands are configured; not introduced by the title callback

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Prompt payload length N and number of Copilot turns. One serialization occurs per turn, including turns after naming is complete and configurations where no prompt shell command exists.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One hook execution per submitted turn; separate sessions/chats may execute concurrently. There is no cache or coalescing because each input differs.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is applicable. Title state can make the callback return undefined, but it does not suppress the preceding serialization.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the callback is always supplied and the stringify precedes the potentially empty command loop.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical prompts are small, but large pasted code/log prompts are supported and make the linear copied-byte cost material.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium serialization/allocation regression on every Copilot turn.

Scenarios.Scenario: Session/chat title seeding and utility-model refinement
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Fallback title normalization runs synchronously during ChatTurnStarted before provider send. Utility-model generation and its metadata writes are scheduled asynchronously; active-agent fallback metadata writes are also fire-and-forget, although later eviction/deletion waits for them.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Collapse whitespace and materialize the full prompt as code-point arrays/strings to derive a 40/200-character title
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once for the first message of each newly titled session/chat; O(N) allocated elements/bytes
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Whitespace normalization still scanned the string, but bounded slicing did not create one array element per code point or join the entire suffix

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write automatic title and provenance metadata
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Three writes for one active-agent fallback; up to four around a utility-generated initial title where one final-title write previously sufficed
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Fallback apply did not write source metadata and generated title persistence issued one title write
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fire-and-forget during interaction, but contends with other per-session writes and is drained by lifecycle waits

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Utility-model title completion and optional GitHub issue/PR enrichment
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing bounded generation calls when active-agent mode is disabled; active-agent mode removes these calls
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Utility model generation already ran when enabled by the old flow
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the initial send critical path and cancellable; not a regression introduced by the active path

Scenarios.ScalingInput: First-prompt length N controls normalization allocations; number of newly titled sessions/chats and title refinements controls metadata write count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Title metadata writes are queued through one per-database metadata Sequencer. Utility generation network calls retain their existing cancellation and GitHub-context limiter behavior; active-agent mode skips them.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No normalization cache. In-memory title sets prevent repeated seeding for an already titled live target, so the large-input allocation is once per newly titled session/chat. Metadata writes are not coalesced, including repeated writes of the same source value.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both normalization and persistence call sequences are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The write latency depends on SQLite/filesystem characteristics and prompt sizes vary, but exact write multiplicity and full-input allocations are deterministic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable repeated-write and large-input allocation regressions; the removed utility-model call in active mode is a performance improvement but does not offset these mechanisms on disabled mode or lifecycle paths.

Scenarios.Scenario: Idle eviction and explicit session deletion
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After provider teardown, deletion waits for pending per-session database writes before removing data. Idle eviction now also waits for pending writes before dropping in-memory session/provider state; this is off active interaction unless an unsubscribe immediately triggers eviction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Wait for pending session writes to settle
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per deletion and once per eligible idle eviction; waits over writes already queued for that session
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Deletion/eviction could proceed without draining pending metadata writes
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks deletion completion or eviction, not active turn progress

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Delete per-session data and optional worktree
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One recursive session-data deletion and at most one worktree cleanup per explicit disposal
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same deletion boundaries existed without the preceding drain
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing destructive cleanup path; the new wait precedes it for ordering

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number and duration of pending writes for the one session, amplified by the duplicate title metadata writes. Chat count controls title-state cleanup iteration.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: whenIdle repeatedly waits for the current pending-write set; metadata writes are serialized, so drain time is the sum of queued metadata operations. Re-subscription/restoration checks prevent eviction after the wait.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: openDatabase acquires a ref-counted, lazily initialized database; calling whenIdle alone does not open SQLite when there are no pending writes. Existing live references share the same database object.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the lifecycle sequence; uncertain only in observed queue depth.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Normally the queue is short; duplicate title writes increase it. The wait is intentional for durability, so only the write amplification is reported rather than the cleanup ordering itself.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate cleanup-lifecycle finding: waiting is a justified ordering constraint, while the avoidable queue growth is captured by the repeated-write finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Provider tool advertisement/materialization across Copilot, Claude, and Codex
Scenarios.CriticalPath: When a provider session is materialized, server-tool definitions are filtered by the current setting and stored on session state. Prompt-time host instructions are then projected through provider-specific mechanisms: Copilot/Claude hooks or Codex turn/start additionalContext.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Codex turn/start request with optional additionalContext
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing IPC request per turn; the diff adds a small field only on rename-reminder turns
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same turn/start IPC occurred without the field
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No additional boundary call, only bounded payload growth

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One callback per Claude prompt; joins at most the small host-instruction list
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Small fixed local callback cost; no subprocess/network operation established

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: O(T) for a small fixed tool count when definitions/toolNames are read

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Small fixed server-tool definition count per materialized session; host instruction count is currently at most one rename reminder.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No new unbounded work in definition filtering. Claude and Copilot execute one in-process prompt hook per turn; Codex adds a fixed additionalContext field to the existing turn/start IPC.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Advertised tools are snapshotted in session state, so later setting changes do not repeatedly rebuild provider sessions. Getter filtering recomputes a small fixed list only at advertisement/access time.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for host-side behavior and boundary count.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider SDK internals may add small hook overhead, but no additional expensive boundary call is evidenced for Claude or Codex.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding beyond Copilot's proven full-prompt serialization; other provider propagation is bounded.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 37 changed files and all diff pages. Submitted four findings: automatic rename catalog-wide boundary fan-out, unconditional Copilot prompt serialization, duplicate title-provenance SQLite writes, and unbounded first-prompt code-point allocation. No concrete shipped-regression fix with blame-worthy prior mechanism was established, so no regression-fix record was filed.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
